subject: Biology
cards: AQA-7402.LOCUS

Define locus.

[1 mark]
(Fixed) position of a gene on DNA (molecule)/chromosome
AQA-7402.EXON

Define exon.

[1 mark]

(Base sequence) coding for amino acid sequence(s)
Ignore: polypeptide chain/protein
AQA-7402.UNIVERSAL_GENETIC_CODE

Define universal genetic code.

[1 mark]

The same codon/triplet (always) codes for the same amino acid
Also accept: 3 bases for triplet/codon
AQA-7402.NON_OVERLAPPING_GENETIC_CODE

Define non-overlapping.

[1 mark]

• Each base is only part of one triplet/codon
• OR
• (Adjacent) codons/triplets do not overlap
Also accept: ‘3 bases’ for triplet
Also accept: ‘base/triplets/codons only read once’
AQA-7402.DEGENERATE_GENETIC_CODE

Define degenerate.

[1 mark]

More than one codon/triplet codes for each amino acid
Also accept: ‘3 bases’ for triplet
AQA-7402.MUTAGENIC_AGENT

Define the term mutagenic agent.

[1 mark]
(A factor that) increases (the rate of) mutations
AQA-7402.QUATERNARY_STRUCTURE_OF_A_PROTEIN

Define the quaternary structure of a protein.

[1 mark]

More than 1 **polypeptide**
Ignore: prosthetic group OR named interactions between chains, eg disulfide bridge
AQA-7402.GENOME

Define genome.

[1 mark]

• Complete set of genes in a cell
• OR
• (All) the DNA in a cell
• OR
• (All) the genes/alleles/genetic material in a cell
• OR
• The total number of DNA bases in a cell
Also accept: organism for cell
Not accepted: ‘all the DNA/genes within a species/population’
AQA-7402.PROTEOME

Define proteome.

[1 mark]

• (Full) range of proteins that a cell **can produce**
• OR
• (Full) range of proteins **coded for** by the cell’s DNA/genome
Also accept: organism for cell
Also accept: For ‘full range’ accept ‘complete set’ OR all
Not accepted: ‘number of proteins’ unqualified
Ignore: ‘range of proteins that a species/population can produce’
AQA-7402.SPECIES

Define species.

[1 mark]
(A group of) organisms that are able to produce fertile offspring
AQA-7402.SPECIES_RICHNESS

What is meant by ‘species richness’?

[1 mark]

(A measure of) the number of (different) species in a community
Also accept: For ‘community’ accept ‘habitat/ecosystem/one area/environment’
Not accepted: ‘in a population’
AQA-7402.GENETIC_DIVERSITY

What is meant by genetic diversity?

[1 mark]

Number of different alleles of each gene
Also accept: number of different base sequences (found) in each gene
AQA-7402.PHENOTYPE

Explain what is meant by the term phenotype.

[2 marks]

• Expression/appearance/characteristic/feature/trait due to genetic constitution / genotype /allele(s)
• (And due to interaction with the) environment
Also accept: named characteristic
Also accept: homozygous/heterozygous/genes/DNA for ‘genotype’
Ignore: chromosomes
AQA-7402.POPULATION

Define the biological term population.

[2 marks]

• A group (of organisms) of the same species in a (particular) space at a (particular) time
• That can (potentially) interbreed
Also accept: descriptions of ‘space’ eg area, part of the world, habitat, ecosystem
Also accept: that can produce fertile offspring
AQA-7402.R_3_1_1_MONOMER

What is a monomer?

[1 mark]

(a monomer is a smaller / repeating) unit / molecule from which larger molecules / polymers are made
Not accepted: atoms / elements / ‘building blocks’ for units / molecules
Ignore: examples
AQA-7402.R_3_3_1_LARGE_ANIMALS_O2_SYSTEM

Explain the advantage for larger animals of having a specialised system that facilitates oxygen uptake.

[2 marks]

• Large(r) organisms have a small(er) surface area:volume (ratio) OR Small(er) organisms have a large(r) surface area:volume (ratio)
• Overcomes long **diffusion** pathway OR Faster **diffusion**
Also accept: short diffusion pathway
Also accept: for ‘faster’, more
AQA-7402.R_3_3_1_SAV_METABOLIC_RATE

Describe and explain the relationship between surface area to volume ratio of the human body and metabolic rate.

[3 marks]

• As surface area to volume ratio increases, metabolic rate increases OR (Humans with) a large surface area to volume ratio have a high/fast metabolic rate
• (A large(r) surface area to volume ratio will) lose **more** heat
• (A high(er) rate of metabolism/respiration) releases/provides/replaces heat OR (A high(er) rate of metabolism/respiration) maintains body temperature
Also accept: the converse for all marking points
Also accept: the relationship is proportional
Also accept: the relationship is positively correlated
Also accept: lose heat faster/more easily
Also accept: (a higher rate of metabolism/respiration) releases energy OR produces/generates heat
Not accepted: produces energy/ heat energy
Ignore: ‘directly’ if prefixing proportional
AQA-7402.R_3_3_1_SIZE_SAV_RELATIONSHIP

Describe the relationship between size and surface area to volume ratio of organisms.

[1 mark]

As size increases, ratio (of surface area to volume) decreases
Also accept: converse
Note: Comparison required, e.g., smaller organisms have a larger ratio
AQA-7402.R_3_3_1_OXYGEN_UPTAKE_METABOLIC_RATE

Explain why oxygen uptake is a measure of metabolic rate in organisms.

[1 mark]

(Oxygen used in) respiration, **which** provides energy / ATP OR (Oxygen is used in) respiration, **which** is a metabolic process / chemical reaction
Not accepted: produces energy
Not accepted: references to anaerobic respiration
AQA-7402.R_3_5_1_LIGHT_INDEPENDENT_PRODUCTS

Describe how the products of the light-dependent reaction are used in the light-independent reaction to produce triose phosphate. Do not include the role of ribulose bisphosphate (RuBP) in your answer.

[3 marks]

• ATP and reduced NADP
• ATP provides **energy**
• GP reduced to triose phosphate
Also accept: NADPH or NADPH2 or NADP + H for reduced NADP.
Also accept: TP for triose phosphate as triose phosphate is named in the question.
Note: Must have idea of reduction. This may be conveyed by stating GP converted to triose phosphate using reduced NADP.
Note: If GP named it must be correct.
AQA-7402.R_3_5_2_GLYCOLYSIS_PROCESS

Describe the process of glycolysis.

[4 marks]

• Phosphorylation of glucose using ATP
• Oxidation of **triose** **phosphate** to pyruvate
• Net gain of ATP
• NAD reduced
Also accept: all mark points in diagrams.
Also accept: removal of hydrogen from triose phosphate for oxidation.
Also accept: any description that indicates a net gain e.g., 4 produced, 2 used.
Also accept: NADH/NADH2/NADH + H+ produced.
AQA-7402.R_3_5_2_MALONATE_OXYGEN_UPTAKE

Malonate inhibits a reaction in the Krebs cycle. Explain why malonate would decrease the uptake of oxygen in a respiring cell.

[2 marks]

• Less/no reduced NAD/coenzymes OR Fewer/no hydrogens/electrons removed (and passed to electron transfer chain)
• Oxygen is the final/terminal (electron) acceptor
Also accept: less/no FAD reduced.
AQA-7402.R_3_5_3_CATTLE_ENERGY_TRANSFER

Farming cattle for humans to eat is less efficient than farming crops because of energy transfer. Explain why.

[2 marks]

• Energy lost between/at trophic/feeding levels
• Energy lost via respiration/excretion/faeces
Also accept: description of trophic levels e.g., food chain.
Also accept: energy lost via heat/metabolism/food not eaten/digested/muscle contraction/movement/maintaining temperature.
Not accepted: energy used in respiration.
Not accepted: energy produced/generated.
AQA-7402.R_3_5_3_ENERGY_LOSS_SECONDARY_TERTIARY

Give three reasons for the low efficiency of energy transfer from secondary consumers to tertiary consumers in an ecosystem.

[3 marks]

• Heat (loss) from respiration
• (Food) not digested OR Not all eaten
• Excretion
Also accept: faeces for not digested.
Also accept: urine/urea for excretion.
AQA-7402.R_3_6_1_EXERCISE_HEART_RATE_RECEPTORS

Exercise causes an increase in heart rate. Describe the role of receptors and of the nervous system in this process.

[4 marks]

• Chemoreceptors detect rise in CO2/H+/acidity/carbonic acid/fall in pH OR Baro/pressure receptors detect rise in blood pressure
• Send impulses to cardiac centre/medulla
• More impulses to SAN
• By sympathetic (nervous system for chemoreceptors/CO2) OR By parasympathetic (nervous system for baro/pressure receptors/blood pressure)
Also accept: action potentials.
Not accepted: ‘messages’, ‘signals’, ‘an impulse’ or an ‘action potential’.
Ignore: location of receptors.
Ignore: chemoreceptors detect oxygen.
Ignore: ‘messages’, ‘signals’, ‘an impulse’ or an ‘action potential’ as emphasis here is on increase in frequency.
AQA-7402.R_3_7_2_GENE_POOL

What is a gene pool?

[1 mark]

All the **alleles** in a population
Also accept: The number of alleles in a population.
Note: All or number of **alleles** in a species on its own is not enough on its own.
AQA-7402.R_3_7_3_CEL_NATURAL_SELECTION

Mammals feed their young on milk. CEL digests the triglycerides in milk. The ability to produce CEL occurred due to a gene mutation. Describe how natural selection may have led to all mammals in a population producing CEL.

[4 marks]

• Mutation results in (a new) allele
• Those with the (new) allele able to digest milk/triglycerides
• Individuals with CEL/allele more likely to (survive and) reproduce
• Directional selection
• Increase in frequency of (this) allele in population
Also accept: ECF for use of gene rather than allele after not awarding mark in the first instance but max 3 overall.
Also accept: ‘pass on allele/characteristic’ for reproduce
Also accept: description of increasing frequency, eg ‘more common’, ‘higher proportion’ but ignore increase in number of allele
Also accept: ‘mutation’ for allele
AQA-7402.R_3_7_3_MALARIA_RESISTANCE_SELECTION

In Africa today, most of the human population are resistant to malaria caused by P. vivax. Use your knowledge of natural selection to explain why this resistance is so common in Africa.

[4 marks]

• Mutation produced **allele**
• Those with allele/resistance less likely to/do not get malaria/P vivax OR Those with allele/resistance survive malaria/P vivax
• (So more likely to) reproduce and pass on the allele
• (Over generations) allele frequency increases
Also accept: converse; eg ‘people lacking the allele die from malaria’
Also accept: description of increasing frequency of allele eg ‘higher proportion’, ‘more common’ but ‘ignore increase in number of allele’
Not accepted: gene for allele only once
Not accepted: ‘mutation caused by infection/exposure to P. vivax’.
AQA-7402.R_3_7_2_HARDY_WEINBERG_AUTOIMMUNE

In mice, one type of autoimmune disease is inherited as a dominant allele. Would the Hardy-Weinberg principle hold true for a population of mice, some of which had this autoimmune disease? Explain your answer.

[2 marks]

• No - no mark
• Mice with autoimmune disease will be unlikely to reproduce/survive OR Mice with autoimmune disease will be selected against
• Will not pass on allele (for autoimmune disease) OR Allele frequency (for autoimmune disease) will reduce/change
• Yes - no mark
• As long as the autoimmune disease did not affect the mice’s ability to reproduce/survive
• The allele frequency will remain constant/not change
AQA-7402.R_3_8_3_PROTEOME_BACTERIA_PROTECTION

Determining the proteomes of bacteria has helped provide protection for individuals and populations against some infectious diseases. Explain how.

[2 marks]

• (Identification/isolation of) **antigens**
• (Antigens/proteins used to develop) vaccines/antitoxins/antiserums OR (Antigens/proteins used) to develop (monoclonal) antibodies
Also accept: descriptions of (active) immunity
Ignore: antibiotics
AQA-7402.R_3_8_3_ECOLI_PROTEOME_EASIER

The analysis of the genome of E. coli allows the proteome to be determined more easily than that of eukaryotes. Explain why.

[2 marks]

• (E. coli / prokaryotes/bacteria) do not have introns /non-coding (DNA) OR (E. coli / prokaryotes/bacteria) only have exons / coding (DNA) OR Eukaryotes contain introns / non-coding (DNA)
• Eukaryotes contain (more) regulatory genes
Also accept: ‘It’ refers to E. coli
Also accept: prokaryotes have no/fewer regulatory genes
AQA-7402.R_3_1_2_STARCH_STORAGE_FEATURES

In the storage tissues of plants, carbohydrates transported through the phloem can be converted into starch. Explain three features of starch that make it a good storage molecule.

[3 marks]

• Insoluble (in water), **so** doesn’t affect water potential/osmosis
• Coiled/spiral/(α-)helix, **so** compact OR Coiled/spiral/(α-)helix **so** can fit many (molecules) in small area
• Many (α-)glucose **for** respiration
• Branched/more ends **so** fast breakdown/hydrolysis
• Large (molecule), **so** can’t leave the cell
Also accept: branched **so** glucose readily released
Also accept: Ψ for water potential
Ignore: surface area
AQA-7402.R_3_1_2_GLYCOGEN_STRUCTURE_FUNCTION

Describe how the structure of glycogen is related to its function.

[4 marks]

• Helix/coiled/branched so compact
• Polymer of glucose so easily hydrolysed
• Branched so more ends for faster hydrolysis
• Glucose (polymer) so provides respiratory substrate for energy (release)
• Insoluble so not (easily) lost (from cell) OR Insoluble so does not affect water potential/osmosis
Also accept: description of ‘compact’, eg many glucoses packed closely/densely/tightly
AQA-7402.R_3_1_2_GOS_POLYSACCHARIDE

Galacto-oligosaccharides (GOS) are polymers of galactose. Explain why GOS are described as polysaccharides.

[2 marks]

Any **two** from:
• Galactose is a monosaccharide/monomer
• (Polysaccharide is a) **carbohydrate** polymer
• (Several) monosaccharides/monomers/galactose joined by **condensation** reactions OR (Several) monosaccharides/monomers/galactose joined by **glycosidic** bonds
AQA-7402.R_3_1_2_DISACCHARIDE_FORMULA_FORMATION

Alpha-gal is a disaccharide found in red meat. Alpha-gal is made of two galactose molecules. Galactose has the chemical formula C6H12O6. Give the chemical formula for the disaccharide, alpha-gal, and describe how it is formed from two galactose molecules.

[2 marks]

• C12H22O11
• Condensation reaction OR With a glycosidic bond
Not accepted: if any other named reaction or named bond given.
Not accepted: if reaction includes addition of water.
Not accepted: answers relating to other carbohydrates.
AQA-7402.R_3_1_2_CELLULOSE_GLYCOGEN_DIFFERENCES

Glycogen and cellulose are both carbohydrates. Describe two differences between the structure of a cellulose molecule and a glycogen molecule.

[2 marks]

• Cellulose is made up of β-glucose (monomers) **and** glycogen is made up of α-glucose (monomers)
• Cellulose molecule has straight chain **and** glycogen is branched
• Cellulose molecule has straight chain **and** glycogen is coiled
• Glycogen has 1,4- and 1,6- glycosidic bonds **and** cellulose has only 1,4- glycosidic bonds
Ignore: ref. to H bonds / microfibrils
AQA-7402.R_3_1_2_SUCROSE_HYDROLYSIS_PRODUCTS

Name the products of the hydrolysis of sucrose.

[2 marks]

• Glucose
• Fructose
Also accept: answers in either order
Ignore: α and β glucose
AQA-7402.R_3_1_2_LACTOSE_FORMATION_GOLGI

Mucus also contains glycoproteins. One of these glycoproteins is a polypeptide with the sugar, lactose, attached. Describe how lactose is formed and where in the cell it would be attached to a polypeptide to form a glycoprotein.

[4 marks]

• Glucose **and** galactose
• Joined by condensation (reaction)
• Joined by glycosidic bond
• Added to polypeptide in Golgi (apparatus)
Ignore: α or β for glucose
AQA-7402.R_3_1_3_PHOSPHOLIPID_BILAYER_TRIGLYCERIDE

Explain why phospholipids can form a bilayer but triglycerides cannot.

[3 marks]

• Phospholipid both hydrophobic and hydrophilic OR Phospholipid polar OR Phosphate group is charged
• Triglycerides only hydrophobic OR Fatty acid/triglyceride is non-polar
• Hydrophilic/phosphate group attracts water (to either side of bilayer)
Also accept: ‘Triglycerides not hydrophilic’
Also accept: ‘faces water’ for ‘attracts water’
Ignore: ‘fatty acids repel water’
AQA-7402.R_3_1_3_LIPID_EMULSION_TEST

Describe how you would test for the presence of a lipid in a liquid sample of food.

[2 marks]

• Add ethanol/alcohol **then** add water **and** shake/mix OR Add ethanol/alcohol **and** shake/mix **then** pour into/add water
• White/milky (emulsion) OR (emulsion) test turns white/milky
Also accept: ‘Add Sudan III and mix’
Also accept: (for Sudan III) top (layer) red
Not accepted: heating the emulsion test
Not accepted: precipitate
Ignore: a second shake
Ignore: cloudy
AQA-7402.R_3_1_3_TRIGLYCERIDE_PHOSPHOLIPID_DIFFERENCE

Describe the difference between the structure of a triglyceride molecule and the structure of a phospholipid molecule.

[1 mark]

In phospholipid, one fatty acid replaced by a phosphate
Also accept: annotated diagrams
Also accept: Pi/PO4 3- / (P)
Not accepted: P/Phosphorus
Ignore: references to saturated and unsaturated
AQA-7402.R_3_1_4_PRIMARY_STRUCTURE_FORMATION

Describe how monomers join to form the primary structure of a protein.

[3 marks]

• Condensation reaction between amino acids
• (Forming) peptide bonds
• Creating (specific) sequence/order of amino acids
Also accept: descriptions of condensation reaction: eg loss of water
AQA-7402.R_3_1_4_PRIMARY_STRUCTURE_DESCRIBE

Describe the primary structure of all proteins.

[2 marks]

• Sequence/order of amino acids
• (Joined by) peptide bonds
AQA-7402.R_3_1_4_BIURET_TEST_PROTEIN

Describe a biochemical test to confirm the presence of protein in a solution.

[2 marks]

• Add biuret (reagent)
• (Positive result) purple/lilac/violet /mauve
Also accept: sodium hydroxide (solution) and copper sulphate (solution)
Not accepted: addition of other incorrect chemicals
Not accepted: other colours
Ignore: references to heating
AQA-7402.R_3_1_4_NONCOMPETITIVE_INHIBITOR_RATE

A non-competitive inhibitor decreases the rate of an enzyme-controlled reaction. Explain how.

[3 marks]

• (Inhibitor) binds (to enzyme) away from active site OR (Inhibitor) does not bind to active site
• Changing (enzyme) tertiary structure OR Changing active site (shape)
• No/fewer enzyme-substrate complexes (form) OR Enzyme-substrate not complementary
Also accept: binds to allosteric (binding) site for does not bind to active site
Also accept: a description of enzyme-substrate complex, eg so no/fewer substrate molecules fit/bind/enter (the active site)
Also accept: no/fewer E-S complexes
Ignore: inhibitor not similar or not same shape as substrate
AQA-7402.R_3_1_4_AMYLASE_NOT_DIGEST_GOS

Explain why amylase produced in the human digestive system does not digest GOS.

[2 marks]

• Active site (only) **complementary** to starch OR Active site not **complementary** to GOS
• (Due to) tertiary structure
Ignore: ‘hydrolysis’
AQA-7402.R_3_1_4_TOXIN_BINDS_ONLY_ILEUM_CELLS

V. cholerae produces a toxin that only binds to the cell-surface membrane of epithelial cells lining the ileum. The toxin is a protein. Explain why the toxin can only bind to the cell-surface membrane of epithelial cells in the ileum.

[2 marks]

• Has (specific) **tertiary** structure/shape
• Structures are **complementary**
Also accept: in context of receptor or toxin
Also accept: in correct context of receptor and/or toxin in relation to MP1
Not accepted: only once reference to active site/enzyme/substrate/induced fit/antibody
Ignore: 3D shape
AQA-7402.R_3_1_4_DIFFERENT_SEQUENCES_SAME_REACTION

Two enzymes, P and Q, are proteins with quaternary structure which catalyse the same reaction, but they have different amino acid sequences. Explain how two enzymes with different amino acid sequences can catalyse the same reaction.

[2 marks]

• (Both) active sites have similar/identical tertiary structures OR (Both) active sites have identical amino acid sequences
• (So) form enzyme-substrate complexes (with the same substrate)
Also accept: (both) have active sites that are complementary to different parts of the substrate;
Also accept: attach/bind for complementary
Also accept: E-S for enzyme-substrate
Ignore: shape for tertiary structure
AQA-7402.R_3_1_4_INDUCED_FIT_CATALYST

Describe the induced-fit model of enzyme action and how an enzyme acts as a catalyst.

[3 marks]

• Substrate binds to the active site/enzyme OR Enzyme-substrate complex forms
• Active site changes shape (slightly) so it is **complementary** to substrate OR Active site changes shape (slightly) so distorting/breaking/forming bonds in the substrate
• Reduces activation energy
Also accept: for ‘binds’, fits
AQA-7402.R_3_1_4_INDUCED_FIT_MODEL

Describe the induced-fit model of enzyme action.

[2 marks]

• (before reaction) active site not complementary to/does not fit substrate
• Shape of active site changes as substrate binds/as enzyme-substrate complex forms
• Stressing/distorting/bending bonds (in substrate leading to reaction)
Ignore: references to how shape change is caused
Note: Points 1 and 2 may be made in one statement and ‘complementary’ introduced at any point.
Note: Points 1&2 - active site mentioned once applies for both points
AQA-7402.R_3_1_4_ACTIVE_SITE_HIGH_RATE

Explain how the active site of an enzyme causes a high rate of reaction.

[3 marks]

• Lowers activation energy
• Induced fit **causes** active site (of enzyme) to change shape
• (So) enzyme-substrate complex **causes** bonds to form/break
Also accept: description, of induced fit
Also accept: enzyme-substrate complex causes stress/strain on bonds.
AQA-7402.R_3_1_4_PEPTIDE_BOND_FORMATION

Describe how a peptide bond is formed between two amino acids to form a dipeptide.

[2 marks]

• Condensation (reaction) / loss of water
• Between amine / NH2 and carboxyl / COOH
Also accept: each marking point if shown clearly in diagram.
Also accept: between amino (group) and carboxylic / acid (group)
AQA-7402.R_3_1_5_PHOSPHODIESTER_BOND_FORMATION

Describe how a phosphodiester bond is formed between two nucleotides within a DNA molecule.

[2 marks]

• Condensation (reaction)/loss of water
• (Between) phosphate **and** deoxyribose
• (Catalysed by) DNA polymerase
Not accepted: if DNA polymerase joins AT/GC OR complementary nucleotides/bases OR forms hydrogen bonds
AQA-7402.R_3_1_6_ATP_PHOSPHATE_RELEASE_USE

Describe how phosphate is released from ATP within cells. Explain one way in which this phosphate can be used by cells.

[3 marks]

• Hydrolysis
• ATP hydrolase
• Phosphorylate other substances **to** make them more reactive/change their shape OR To form DNA/RNA/phospholipids
Also accept: ATPase
Also accept: description of phosphorylation
Also accept: any named biological molecule containing phosphate e.g. triose phosphate
Not accepted: hydrolysis of hydrogen bond
Ignore: other named bonds
Ignore: to form ATP
AQA-7402.R_3_1_6_ATP_FORMATION_COMPONENTS

Describe how an ATP molecule is formed from its component molecules.

[4 marks]

• Accept for 2 marks correct names of three components adenine, ribose/pentose, **three** phosphates
• Condensation (reaction)
• ATP synthase
Also accept: for 1 mark, correct name of two components
Also accept: for 1 mark, ADP and phosphate/Pi
Also accept: suitably labelled diagram
Not accepted: ATPase
Ignore: adenosine
Ignore: phosphodiester
AQA-7402.R_3_1_6_ATP_STRUCTURE_BREAKDOWN

Describe the structure of ATP. Outline how named enzymes break down and resynthesise ATP.

[4 marks]

• Ribose, Adenine **and** 3 phosphates
• ATP to ADP + Pi by ATP hydrolase in hydrolysis (reaction)
• ADP + Pi to ATP by ATP synthase
• (In) condensation (reaction)
Also accept: a labelled diagram showing ribose, adenine and 3 phosphates
Also accept: adenosine and 3 phosphates
Also accept: ATPase for ATP hydrolase
Also accept: hydrolayse
Also accept: synthayse
Not accepted: Adenosine and 3 phosphates if ribose/pentose is also mentioned
Ignore: pentose sugar
AQA-7402.R_3_1_6_ATP_RESYNTHESIS

Cells constantly hydrolyse ATP to provide energy. Describe how ATP is resynthesised in cells.

[2 marks]

• From ADP and phosphate
• By ATP synthase
• During respiration/photosynthesis
Also accept: Pi/PO4 3- / (P)
Not accepted: P/Phosphorus
Not accepted: use of water in the reaction
AQA-7402.R_3_1_7_WATER_PROPERTIES_IMPORTANCE

Water has a high heat capacity and a large latent heat of vaporisation. Describe the importance of each of these properties to living organisms.

[2 marks]

• Buffers changes in temperature
• (Provides a) cooling effect (via evaporation)
Also accept: descriptions of buffering changes in temperature, eg resists temperature changes
AQA-7402.R_3_1_8_IRON_ION_PROPERTY

Explain a property of iron ions that enables these ions to carry out their role in red blood cells.

[2 marks]

• (Is) charged/polar OR (Is) part of haem(oglobin)
• (So) binds/associates/loads (with) oxygen OR (So) forms oxyhaemoglobin OR (So) transports oxygen
Also accept: Fe 2+ OR Fe 3+ for ‘charged’
Also accept: ‘carries’ for transports
AQA-7402.R_3_1_8_HYDROGEN_IONS_PLASMA_PROTEINS

Diseased lungs can cause carbon dioxide to build up in the blood plasma. This leads to an increase in hydrogen ion concentration in the plasma. Describe the effect this increase in hydrogen ion concentration has on the plasma and on the proteins in the plasma. Do not refer to the Bohr effect.

[2 marks]

• Increased (plasma) acidity OR Decreased (plasma) pH
• Denatures (protein) OR Changes (protein) tertiary structure OR Changes active site (shape) OR Changes antigen-binding site (shape)
Also accept: description of bond changes, eg ‘disrupts hydrogen/ ionic bonds’ for ‘changes in tertiary structure’
AQA-7402.R_3_2_1_CHLOROPLAST_FRACTIONATION

Describe how you would use cell fractionation techniques to obtain a sample of chloroplasts from leaf tissue. Do not include in your answer information about any solutions.

[3 marks]

• Macerate / homogenise / blend / break tissues / cells (in solution)
• Centrifuge
• At different / increasing speeds until chloroplast fraction obtained
Also accept: any suitable method to break tissues / cells / release organelles
Also accept: ‘perform differential centrifugation until chloroplasts obtained.’ for 2 marks
AQA-7402.R_3_2_1_CHLOROPLAST_ISOLATION

Describe how a sample of chloroplasts could be isolated from leaves.

[4 marks]

• Break open cells/tissue **and** filter OR Grind/blend cells/tissue/leaves **and** filter
• In cold, same water potential/concentration, pH controlled solution
• Centrifuge/spin and remove nuclei/cell debris
• (Centrifuge/spin) at high(er) speed, chloroplasts settle out
Also accept: homogenise and filter
Also accept: for ‘same water potential/concentration’, isotonic
Also accept: for ‘pH controlled’, buffered
AQA-7402.R_3_2_1_PROTEIN_PRODUCTION_ORGANELLES

Eukaryotic cells produce and release proteins. Outline the role of organelles in the production, transport and release of proteins from eukaryotic cells. Do not include details of transcription and translation in your answer.

[4 marks]

• DNA in nucleus is code (for protein)
• Ribosomes/rough endoplasmic reticulum produce (protein)
• Mitochondria produce ATP (for protein synthesis)
• Golgi apparatus package/modify OR Carbohydrate added/glycoprotein produced by Golgi apparatus
• Vesicles transport OR Rough endoplasmic reticulum transports
• (Vesicles) fuse with cell(-surface) membrane
Also accept: rER for ‘rough endoplasmic reticulum’
Also accept: body for ‘apparatus’
Also accept: exocytosis at cell membrane
AQA-7402.R_3_2_1_CHLOROPLAST_MITOCHONDRION_COMPARE
